text:
alice: paging oncall — seeing sustained queue growth for tenant `vanguard` in dedicated-usw-2 pool. dashboard shows TenantQueueDepth ~1.2k, 95p latency ~5.2s, some 503s. Noticing large mixed-size requests. Anyone oncall?
incident-bot: [ALERT] tenant_queue_depth_high - tenant=vanguard pool=d-pool-usw-2 threshold=1000 — triggered at 1813456789
kendra: oncall here. thanks alice. is this affecting other tenants?
alice: no, isolated to vanguard dedicated pool. other tenants normal.
chris: copying perf metrics — looks like a handful of long prompts (20k token user jobs) interleaving with short ones. big batches are forming and holding up queues.
sam: if big requests are dominating batch windows we should try a per-tenant batch token cap (max_batch_tokens) to limit head-of-line blocking. can we set vanguard max_batch_tokens lower?
miguel: agree. current global default is 1024 tokens per batch. propose reducing to 256 for vanguard as a quick mitigation.
kendra: risks? more small batches -> more GPU kernel launches and slightly higher CPU overhead, but should drop tail latency and reduce 503s.
alice: customer reported user-facing failures for some API routes, so prioritize.
chris: quick check — can we apply tenant-shaper without rolling infra? there's an on-the-fly knob via infra-cli. iirc: `infra-cli tenants update --id vanguard --set max_batch_tokens=256`
sam: also add a queue_shaper to cap in-flight requests: `infra-cli tenants update --id vanguard --set queue_shaper.burst_limit=300`
kendra: can someone run the command now? i'll own monitoring and pager duty followups.
miguel: running `infra-cli` now — pushing to the control plane.

# command run by miguel
infra-cli tenants update --id vanguard \
  --set max_batch_tokens=256 \
  --set queue_shaper.burst_limit=300 \
  --set queue_shaper.mode=latency
```

miguel: control plane accepted the change, pushing to d-pool-usw-2. patch id=chg-3387
chris: confirming rollout to nodes — 6/6 agents acknowledged, applying config.
incident-bot: [CONFIG_CHANGE] tenant_config_update - tenant=vanguard change=chg-3387 by=miguel at 1813456895

kendra: watching metrics now. queue depth dropping from 1.2k -> 420 in ~60s. 95p latency down to 800ms. still some 503s but tapering.
alice: customer on slack said some requests recovered. good sign.
sam: nice. follow-up: we should also consider per-route sampling to detect long-running prompts and throttling them at the edge.
miguel: logged a short-term follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IOPS-1123 — investigate per-route pre-emptive shaping.
chris: for completeness, pasted current effective tenant knobs:
```
max_batch_tokens: 256
queue_shaper:
  mode: latency
  burst_limit: 300
  sustained_limit: 100
```

kendra: agreed next steps: 1) keep these shaper knobs for 2 hours monitoring 2) if stable, promote to a 24h temporary policy and notify the customer 3) schedule a deeper perf review with research and runtime team tomorrow.

alice: handoff — i'm going offline in ~30m, kendra will keep owning. tagging @oncall-next for awareness.
kendra: taking over. sam, can you help with a small canary to gradually relax the knob if load normalizes? want to avoid oscillation.
sam: yep — i'll script a canary that steps max_batch_tokens 256->512 in 3 min increments if queue depth < 50 for 5 consecutive minutes. pushing to ops-runbooks.

chris: note for postmortem: tenant ran a burst of mixed long/short jobs during business hours; dedicated pool means isolation but requires bespoke shaper. add recommended defaults to docs: per-tenant max_batch_tokens and queue_shaper guidance.
miguel: creating an internal incident thread and linking to customer ticket. will include the `infra-cli` commands used + monitoring graphs.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE_POSSIBLE] queue_depth_drop_detected - tenant=vanguard current=120 last=420 triggered at 1813457010 — monitor for 30m
kendra: closing the page for now. keeping the thread open for notes and follow-ups. thanks all :thumbsup:
